note: Codes are the deposit's own column names (data/yoshimura_2026_psych_safety.py melts ps3m1..ps3m9 unchanged). The deposit carries no item text: the S1 Codebook labels them only 'Psychological safety item 1..9' (1-7). The paper (Methods 2.3.3) says PS was measured with 'the Japanese version of the scale in [28] [O'Donovan et al. 2020], adapted and validated in [30] [Sasaki et al. 2022]', using 'only the leader psychological safety subscale', nine items on a seven-point scale, example 'When I express my opinion, the team leader [or supervisor] listens to it with respect' - which is a back-rendering of Sasaki's Japanese Section 1 item 7 (私が自分の意見を言うと、チームのリーダー（または上司）はその意見を尊重して聞いてくれる), not of O'Donovan's English item 7 ('...my input is valued by my team leader'). Sasaki's Section 1 has exactly nine team-leader items on 1-7, matching ps3m1-9. item_text = Sasaki Supplement Section 1 items 1-9, Japanese from the PDF text layer (checked against a page render; leading '１．' numbering stripped, line-wrap joins removed). Yoshimura's own administered questionnaire is not in the deposit (S1 Dataset .xlsx, S1 Codebook .docx) or supplements (S1 Table .docx, S1 File .pdf), so the wording is the published Japanese version, not a copy of this study's form. instructions = the supplement's general instruction plus the Section 1 prompt (Japanese), since this table carries Section 1 only; whether Yoshimura's form used identical framing is not known. English (item_text_translated, instructions_translated, option_text_translated) is the parallel English printed in the same supplement (O'Donovan's original items; matches Sasaki Table 3) - official_instrument_english: a parallel version, so item 7 English ('input is valued') does not correspond word-for-word to the Japanese ('listens with respect'). option_text: only anchors 1 (全くそう思わない / strongly disagree) and 7 (非常にそう思う / strongly agree) are labelled in the source; 2-6 left blank. Alignment of ps3m<k> to Sasaki Section 1 item k is inferred from numbering (paper_order). Rights: no register row for this instrument; Sasaki 2022 and O'Donovan et al. 2020 (BMC Med Res Methodol, PMC7387873) are both CC BY 4.0 and neither states a restriction on the scale (text scanned for permission/non-commercial/contact clauses: none beyond the CC licence boilerplate) - silence, not a block. Step 3b: no mismatch; dictionary Description 'Psychological safety scale, 9 items, 1-7' is correct and could add 'leader subscale (Sasaki 2022 Japanese version of O'Donovan 2020)'.
